Hi Maria —

Thanks for the clear list — below is a concise, procurement-friendly statement followed by an expanded technical appendix. Please let me know if you want any edits for legal language.

Concise statement (one paragraph):
Redwood Inference does not use customer data to train models. For the Hosted API, request and response bodies (prompts and model outputs) are retained by default for 30 days to enable debugging, abuse monitoring, and quality reviews; metadata and logs are retained for 365 days. Customers on our "Privacy Add-on" or enterprise Dedicated offerings can opt into zero-retention configurations; Dedicated and Private deployments allow customers to configure no retention such that Redwood does not persist request/response bodies outside the customer's controlled environment. All data in transit and at rest is encrypted (TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest); keys may be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Expanded technical appendix (short):
- Hosted API (default):
  - Prompts & outputs: persisted encrypted in region-specific buckets for 30 days by default; short-term caching in-memory for inference but not persisted beyond the configured retention window.
  - Logs & metadata (request IDs, timestamps, model metrics): retained 365 days for operational and security auditing.
  - Embeddings: stored only if explicitly requested by the customer (e.g., for semantic search); retention follows the same configurable policy and can be deleted on request.
  - Data residency: customers may select regional endpoints (US/EU) — data stored in the selected region.
  - Opt-out: a paid Privacy Add-on is available that disables storage of request/response bodies (zero retention) for Hosted traffic; note that some operational logs may still be retained in aggregated/anonymized form for system health and security.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Deployment options allow retention policies to be set by the customer. We offer a configuration with zero retention where Redwood does not persist request/response bodies outside of ephemeral inference nodes. Keys can be customer-managed.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Redwood software runs in the customer's environment; by default Redwood does not collect or store request/response bodies. All storage is under customer control.

- Security controls & certifications:
  - All persisted data is encrypted at rest with AES-256; TLS 1.2+ in transit.
  - Support for customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated/Private.
  - SOC 2 Type II report available on request (attached).

If helpful, we can produce a one-page PDF with the concise paragraph and a 3-line FAQ for Procurement / Legal that references our SOC2 and the Privacy Add-on order form. I've attached the SOC2 PDF and our data-handling FAQ.

-Neha
